1	# Tier 5: the differential tasks and what the product loop did with them
2	
3	Ten tasks whose main check runs the candidate on cases held in `reference/cases.json`, which no workspace receives. Each is a command, `src/cli.js`, driven by arguments and standard input and judged on its exit code and its two streams; the visible `test/*.test.js` covers the main paths only, and the rest of the verdict comes from the hidden corpus. The rationale and the design are in [the tier-5 Agent Note](../../../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-07-bench-tier-5-hidden-cases.md).
4	
5	## The tasks
6	
7	| Task | Domain | Held out | Visible assertions | Hidden cases | Reference lines | What it turns on |
8	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
9	| `uri-resolve` | parsing | no | 16 | 150 | 255 | Percent-encodings normalize before dot segments are removed, so `%2E%2E` climbs; a default port must be written with exactly the default's digits to be dropped. |
10	| `glob-brace` | parsing | yes | 17 | 170 | 406 | Extended groups divide the segment every way, brace ranges pad and count down, and a leading `.` needs a literal `.` to match. |
11	| `conf-canon` | parsing | no | 18 | 150 | 339 | Which header may redeclare which table, where a dotted key may walk, and fifteen distinct failure messages. |
12	| `build-schedule` | data-structures-algorithms | no | 15 | 140 | 287 | List scheduling by longest remaining chain, a zero-cost task freeing its worker in the instant it starts, and one named cycle out of many. |
13	| `ranked-choice` | data-structures-algorithms | no | 16 | 170 | 170 | The backwards tie-break restarts from the first round after each narrowing, and majority is strictly more than half of the ballots still counting. |
14	| `sheet-eval` | data-structures-algorithms | no | 18 | 150 | 464 | Six error tokens with a stated precedence, `IF` hiding the branch it did not take, and a unary sign binding tighter than `^`. |
15	| `lex-states` | state-machines | no | 16 | 160 | 288 | Tab-stopped columns, nestable block comments, and a number that runs into a name reporting everything it consumed. |
16	| `rate-limit-sim` | systems | no | 17 | 150 | 230 | Refill accrues as an exact fraction of the period, every routed policy advances before any is asked, and a denied event consumes nothing. |
17	| `diff3-merge` | text | no | 15 | 160 | 187 | The longest common subsequence is pinned to its earliest match, and adjacent changes absorb into one conflict region. |
18	| `wrap-justify` | text | yes | 16 | 160 | 191 | Width counts columns over a stated code-point table, and a word breaks at the last hyphenation point that still fits. |
19	
20	## The difficulty gate
21	
22	Each task was run once against the Claude Code product loop in a copy of its directory with `reference/` removed — `claude -p "<prompt + shared rules>" --permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools "Bash(node:*)" Read Edit Write --no-session-persistence`, eight-minute limit — and what the loop left behind was scored against the visible suite and the hidden cases. `timeout` means the limit cut the attempt off; the loop had written nothing usable by then, which is why those rows score zero on both.
23	
24	Round 1 ran all ten. Round 2 re-ran the six that had passed every hidden case, after their corpora gained corner cases for the specification points listed above; the table reports each task against its shipped corpus, so round 2 for those six and round 1 for the other four.
25	
26	| Task | Visible suite | Hidden cases | Wall time | Round |
27	|---|---|---|---|---|
28	| `uri-resolve` | pass | 150 / 150 | 417 s | 2 |
29	| `glob-brace` | fail | 0 / 170 | 480 s, timeout | 1 |
30	| `conf-canon` | fail | 0 / 150 | 481 s, timeout | 1 |
31	| `build-schedule` | pass | 140 / 140 | 302 s | 2 |
32	| `ranked-choice` | pass | 170 / 170 | 201 s | 2 |
33	| `sheet-eval` | fail | 0 / 150 | 480 s, timeout | 1 |
34	| `lex-states` | pass | 158 / 160 | 367 s | 1 |
35	| `rate-limit-sim` | pass | 150 / 150 | 313 s | 2 |
36	| `diff3-merge` | pass | 160 / 160 | 300 s | 2 |
37	| `wrap-justify` | pass | 160 / 160 | 260 s | 2 |
38	
39	Four tasks failed at least one hidden case and seven passed their visible suite, which is the bar the tier was accepted against. Only `lex-states` failed while its visible suite passed, which is the shape the tier is for; the other three failures are attempts the eight-minute limit cut off. The six re-run tasks scored the same in both rounds — every one of them at every hidden case — so the added corners changed nothing for this implementer, and the tier's separating power against it currently rests on the size of the four hardest specifications rather than on their corners.

data/proving-ground/README.md:288:The thirty-second record is E6, the cascade with a bounded cheap rung, launched at 23:04 UTC on `5ecc68640` and recorded on `9df40295b`, the first experiment run through `pnpm run bench -- experiment` and the first whose arms the service interleaved, so every environment's baseline and candidate cells ran side by side instead of an arm apart: the eight audited tier-5 tasks at two repetitions, seed 2, sealed, 4,307 s of wall time at two cells at a time, the baseline `opus` on three rungs against a candidate whose first rung is `haiku` held to 0.2 of the cell's caps (300,000 billed tokens, 240 s) before `opus`, `opus`, the transcript kept. Both arms certified 16 of 16, so the reading is 0, [0, 0], `inconclusive` by construction. The share did what it was built for: it cut the cheap rung in 14 of 16 cells, 13 at the token share and one at the wall share, as `budget/breach` events scoped to the attempt that blocked no goal, and no cell breached the cell's own caps; the cheap rung certified one cell alone (lex-states, in 129 s), and the strong rung certified the other fifteen, thirteen at the second attempt and two (build-schedule and diff3-merge, one repetition each) at the third. Against the handoff-tax record of 2026-09-08, where the same cascade unbounded certified 14 of 16, the share recovers the two lost certificates; against the strong model alone it recovers none of the cost: 5,618 s of cell time (median 357 s) against 2,802 (median 146 s), 458,300 output tokens against 208,948, 9,231,899 cache-read against 2,542,311, 10,376,073 billed against 2,879,668, because the strong rung's work after the hand-off is a full attempt and the cheap rung's 300,000 tokens buy a certificate in one cell of sixteen. The census finds six cells naming a path outside their workspace in thirteen tool calls, five of them the run directory or a sibling, and no read denied.
data/proving-ground/README.md:290:The thirty-first record is the drop pair frozen as one experiment on the fixed overlay, launched at 21:15 UTC on `14d244cdf` and recorded on `5ecc68640`: the same eight audited tier-5 tasks at two repetitions, seed 2, the same ladder in both arms, `haiku` then `opus`, `opus`, the baseline keeping the transcript on the route and the candidate giving every rung a fresh in-process child, sealed, at two cells at a time. The experiments service still ran the arms in sequence at this launch (the interleaved schedule landed afterwards), so the sixteen baseline cells ran first, and the container this session runs in restarted at 23:00 UTC with nine candidate cells started, two of them before any attempt, and the driver dead before its fold; the record is therefore partial, 25 session logs and 23 cells with at least one attempt, recorded with `--partial` and the reason in its manifest, and its result is the offline fold [folds/2026-09-18-e5-drop-frozen-spawn-against-route-t5.json](folds/2026-09-18-e5-drop-frozen-spawn-against-route-t5.json) over the seven complete pairs, which leaves the two interrupted cells out. The baseline certified 15 of 16, two at the first rung (lex-states, both repetitions) and the rest at the second, its one miss sheet-eval after three attempts at the cap; the candidate certified 5 of the 7 cells that ran an attempt, and its two misses, build-schedule and conf-canon (one repetition each), are again cells whose smallest-model rung alone breached the cell's cap so the strong rung never ran, the allocation defect the per-rung share now closes. The fold reads −0.2857, [−0.5714, 0], `inconclusive`: on build-schedule and conf-canon, two of the three tasks that carried the thirtieth record's flips toward the fresh child, this pair flipped the other way, the kept transcript certifying both repetitions and the fresh child one each, so the offline reading in the drop's favour does not replicate on the frozen pair as far as it ran, and what the fresh child's misses share across both readings is the cap, not the transcript. The baseline spent 497,765 output tokens and 15,214,438 billed over 7,427 s of cell time (median 499 s), the nine candidate sessions 292,596 output tokens and 7,460,089 billed over 4,550 s (median 567 s); the census finds five cells naming a path outside their workspace in eleven tool calls, three of them the run directory or a sibling, and no read denied. The nine candidate cells that never ran, and the pair rerun with the share on the spawn arm, are queued.
data/proving-ground/README.md:292:The thirtieth record is the drop arm run as a fleet under the fixed overlay, launched at 17:43 UTC, eighty minutes after its baseline: the same 16 cells, seed 2, the same ladder, every rung a fresh in-process child of the runner's process on the rung's model with the task restated and the directive carried, the same caps, 5,816 s of wall time at two cells at a time. It certified 14 of 16: 2 at the first rung by the smallest model (ranked-choice, both repetitions), 11 at the second rung by the largest, and 1 at the third (diff3-merge); its two misses (conf-canon and sheet-eval, one repetition each) never reached the strong rung, because the smallest model's single attempt had spent 1,493,040 and 1,472,984 of the cell's 1,500,000 billed tokens rereading its own transcript, and the runner refused the second rung on the breached cap. Folded offline against the twenty-ninth's baseline arm ([folds/2026-09-08-e5-drop-against-kept-transcript-t5.json](folds/2026-09-08-e5-drop-against-kept-transcript-t5.json)), the reading is 0.1875, [0.0625, 0.3125], `promote` by the fold's thresholds: three cells flipped, all toward the fresh child and all on the three tasks the kept transcript failed (build-schedule, conf-canon, sheet-eval), none the other way, with both arms' first rungs at 2 of 16. The fresh child is not cheaper: 575,350 output tokens against 471,583, 16,648,949 billed against 14,911,342, 11,377 s of cell time (median 678 s) against 6,964 (median 441), because every rung reads the task and the workspace from nothing; what it buys is a strong rung that starts from the workspace and the directive instead of from the cheap model's transcript. The fold is offline: its arms ran an hour apart on the shared subscription and were not frozen together, so it is evidence for the slate's prediction that dropping the cheap transcript beats keeping it, not a promotion; the frozen pair on the fixed overlay and a per-rung share of the token cap are queued. The usage of a delegated cell is summed over its `environment/delegation` events, which carry each child's reported model and usage; the census finds no cell leaving its workspace and no read denied.
data/proving-ground/README.md:298:The twenty-seventh record is the handoff tax as a frozen paired experiment on the attempt ladder: the largest product model on three rungs as the baseline against the smallest model on the first rung and the largest on the second and third with the transcript kept, over the eight audited tier-5 environments, seed 2, two repetitions, 32 cells, 5,862 s of wall time at two cells at a time, sealed. The baseline certified 16 of 16 at the first attempt, the fourth such sweep of the largest model on these cells. The ladder certified 14 of 16: the smallest model's first attempt made 2 (lex-states and ranked-choice, one repetition each), the largest model on the second rung recovered 11, the third rung 1 more (diff3-merge), and two cells ran all three attempts out (conf-canon and rate-limit-sim, one repetition each), where the largest model, holding a failed first attempt it did not write, missed twice on tasks it has never missed from a clean start in 64 cells. Delta −0.125, interval [−0.25, 0], inconclusive: two cells in sixteen, at the noise floor, and never above zero. The tax is in the cost, not the verdict. The ladder spent 8,122 s of cell time against 3,251 (medians 531 s against 175), 535 model steps against 181, 500,664 output tokens against 198,637, 1,150,560 cache-write against 328,456, and 14,245,694 cache-read against 2,651,444; the smallest model's rung alone cost 406 steps, 312,430 output tokens, and 9,401,938 cache-read before the largest model ran at all, and the largest model's own share after the handoff (129 steps, 188,234 output tokens) is within a step or a token of what it spends from a clean start (181 and 198,637 here, 164 and 189,169 in the twentieth record), so the inherited transcript saved it nothing. Escalating from the cheap model to the strong one on these tasks recovers most of the certificates the cheap model misses, 12 of 14, and costs two and a half times what starting strong costs on every measure while giving back two certificates. The offline cascade of the twenty-first record priced this order at 4.9 times the largest model's output tokens because it charged the smallest model's whole three-attempt failure before escalating; the ladder escalates after one attempt and pays 2.5 times, so the live reading is cheaper than the offline one and the conclusion is the same, since the strong model's work after the handoff is no cheaper than its own first attempt. The census finds six cells leaving their workspace in eight tool calls, two naming the run directory or a sibling, every one answered by the empty sealed directory, and no read denied.
data/proving-ground/README.md:300:The twenty-sixth record is the downshift arm of the routing hypothesis as a frozen paired experiment on the attempt ladder: the largest product model on three rungs as the baseline against the largest model on the first rung and the smallest on the second and third with the transcript kept, over the eight audited tier-5 environments, seed 2, two repetitions, 32 cells, 3,192 s of wall time at two cells at a time, sealed. The downshift never happened: the largest model certified 16 of 16 at the first attempt in both arms, so no cell reached a rung the smallest model would have run, the two arms are two runs of the same thing, and the fold reads 0, [0, 0], inconclusive by construction. The record is still worth its cells for two readings. It is the second and third first-attempt sweep of the largest model on these cells after the twentieth record (and the baseline arm of the twenty-seventh, running as this is written, is a fourth), so the top of the model order is as repeatable as the middle model's flips are not. And two runs of one arm give the cost noise floor the way three runs of the middle model gave the certificate noise floor: 174,804 against 186,731 output tokens, 291,756 against 307,765 cache-write, 1,894,101 against 2,240,677 cache-read, 146 against 157 model steps, 2,903 against 3,328 s of cell time with the same 156 s median, so a spend difference under 7 percent in output tokens or 15 percent in cell time between two arms of one model is within one arm's own variation. The downshift question, whether the cheap model can finish what the strong one started, cannot be posed on a bench the strong model finishes alone at the first attempt; it needs tasks the largest model itself takes a second attempt on, which no admitted tier holds. The census finds three cells leaving their workspace in four tool calls, none naming the run directory or a sibling, and no read denied.
data/proving-ground/README.md:306:The twenty-third record is the attempt hypothesis as one frozen paired experiment, which the attempt ladder made possible: the runner takes a ladder's length as a run's attempt bound, so the baseline arm ladders three rungs of the middle model and the candidate one rung of the same model on the same route, and the two arms differ in exactly the cap, with no overlay and no offline fold. Over the eight audited tier-5 environments, seed 2, two repetitions, 32 cells, 5,666 s of wall time at two cells at a time, on the sealed composition with continuity, the three-attempt arm certified 15 of 16 (12 at the first attempt, build-schedule, diff3-merge, and lex-states once each at the second, sheet-eval missed once after three) and the one-attempt arm 9 of 16, delta −0.375, interval [−0.5625, −0.1875], verdict reject for the cap of one: the interval clears the 0.0625 noise floor six times over, and it is the first frozen verdict on record about a mechanism of the harness rather than a model. Read the difference in two parts. Three of the sixteen certificates came at a second attempt after a clustered directive, which is the −0.1875 the counterfactual fold of the eleventh record predicted and exactly what a cap of one forfeits. The other three come from the first attempts themselves: the one-attempt arm's first attempts certified 9 of 16 where the three-attempt arm's certified 12, and the first attempt is the same delivery under either ladder (the task statement alone, nothing about the cap reaches the model), so that part is run-to-run variation of first attempts, not an effect of the cap. Cell by cell the two arms' first attempts disagree on nine of sixteen (three the baseline missed and the candidate made, six the other way), while the final outcomes of two three-attempt runs of this arm disagree on one or two; the loop's value is that it absorbs first-attempt variance the tasks produce whatever the cap, and a single-attempt reading of any model on this bench is a noisier instrument than the three-attempt one by that margin. The cap did not buy speed: 5,689 s of cell time against 5,400 (medians 295 s against 300), 240 model steps against 219, 441,504 output tokens against 402,346, so the two later attempts cost 289 s and 39,158 output tokens over sixteen cells for six more certificates. The census finds eight cells naming their parent or the run directory in twelve tool calls, every one answered by the empty sealed directory, and no read denied.
data/proving-ground/README.md:308:The twenty-second record is the eighteenth rerun as the slate meant it: the harness loop as the baseline arm against the product's own loop as the candidate, the same middle model on both, over the eight audited tier-5 environments, seed 2, two repetitions, 32 cells, 7,235 s of wall time at two cells at a time, on the sealed composition with session continuity on the route and, for the first time, the same caps on both arms: 1,500,000 billed tokens (input plus cache read plus cache write, as the budget policy bills every route) and 1,200,000 ms of wall time per cell, applied to a delegated attempt as to the harness's own. The harness loop certified 15 of 16 (14 at the first attempt, conf-canon once at the third, sheet-eval missed once after three attempts); the product loop 14 of 16, every one at its first attempt, delta −0.0625, interval [−0.125, 0], verdict inconclusive, and the delta is one flip, inside the noise floor the twenty-first record measured. What the parity changed is visible in the two product misses: lex-states breached the token cap after one attempt (1,786,072 billed tokens measured against 1,500,000) and sheet-eval the wall cap (1,202,455 ms against 1,200,000), so neither got the second attempt the eighteenth record's uncapped product arm took, and the cell the product loop had recovered there was not recovered here. Under the same caps the harness loop was the faster arm in 15 of 16 pairs, 5,740 s of cell time against 8,187 (medians 255 s against 422), and the cheaper one: 447,289 output tokens and 7,695,132 billed tokens against 625,239 output and 25,817,220 billed on the product side, where the product reported 14.72 USD for its fifteen attempts that reported usage at all. Three of the harness loop's sealed runs on these cells now stand at 15, 14, and 13 of 16, one or two flips apart; the product loop's two runs at 14 and 11, the second of them uncapped and unsealed. Read with the eighth record and the tier-2 and tier-4 fleets, the harness loop is never worse than the product loop on certificates and is faster at tier 2 and tier 5, slower at tier 4, and the difference it makes is not in certificates but in what surrounds them: the caps hold, the record is complete, and the cell is sealed. The census finds seven harness cells naming their parent or the run directory in eight tool calls, every one answered by the empty sealed directory, and no read denied; the product's child runs outside the harness log, so its own calls are not censused.

./packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/README.md:80:`modelOverrides` reshapes individual installed-catalog models without that cost: each key is a catalog model id, each value the same fields a `models` entry takes with the id living in the key, and the rest of the catalog keeps serving untouched — "correct one model, keep the other thirty-seven" as a three-line edit. An override becomes that catalog entry's configuration, so capacities, efforts, and compat resolve through the same path with the same diagnostics and the same request-default semantics as a `models` entry. Most of it was one `createTuiChat` factory: a ~1600-line closure holding roughly forty mutable variables and as many nested closures. Model selection, the ask-user-question queue, and session resume were tangled into that single scope, so a reader could not follow any one concern without holding the whole file in their head, and unrelated edits collided. A prior pass had grouped `src/` into `components/`, `session/`, `extension/`, but the entry file itself and the loose top-level input files (`autocomplete.ts`, `file-autocomplete.ts`, `skill-invocation.ts`, `xml-tool-output.ts`) were untouched.

./.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-03-package-anchored-subsystem-pages.md:9:The [subsystems catalog](2026-06-20-core-data-structures-catalog.md) scoped its front page by the spine-vs-seam rule: a type was "core" if the loop holds, derives, streams, or logs it on every turn. That rule selected types, not packages, so as the folder grew to forty-plus pages the front page became a cross-package grab-bag: LLM conversation vocabulary sat above the agent contracts, the creation/ownership vocabulary (`AgentHandle`, `CreateAgentOptions`, `ResumeAgentOptions`, `AgentFactory`) was documented nowhere in the folder because the generator exempted it to a package README, and a reader could not predict which page documents a type from where the type lives. Package-group READMEs meanwhile had no common shape — some carried sectioned tables, stray design essays, or trailing paragraphs that belonged on a subsystem page.
./.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-03-package-anchored-subsystem-pages.md:25:**A flat single-document catalog.** Already rejected in the [original catalog note](2026-06-20-core-data-structures-catalog.md); the growth to forty-one pages confirmed that verdict.
./.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-05-uniform-agent-note-format.md:30:Every Agent Note now costs slightly more structure, and the mandatory `Alternatives considered` section is deliberate friction: a decision recorded without what it beat invites the re-litigation Agent Notes exist to prevent. Pre-format Agent Notes whose alternatives were not reconstructible carry the grandfather comment permanently — an honest gap on the record rather than fabricated rationale. `doc-sync` gains one gate, and moving an Agent Note between lifecycle folders is now real work at move time (the body rewrite the move always owed) instead of deferred cleanup nothing tracked. The thirty-nine debt markers are gone, resolved by the template they were waiting for.
./.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-06-18-markdown-cross-link-lint.md:11:The motivating case is the Agent Note tree reorganization that introduced this gate: unifying `docs/adr/` + `.agents/notes/` into one `.agents/notes/` with `proposed/`/`implemented/`/`rejected/` subfolders renamed roughly forty inter-doc links by hand. A single fat-fingered path would have shipped a broken link with nothing to catch it.
./.agents/notes/implemented/feature/2026-08-08-pi-ai-per-model-reasoning-declarations.md:11:Two adjacent gaps compounded this. pi-ai decides the reasoning *wire dialect* (`compat.thinkingFormat`, `compat.supportsReasoningEffort`) by recognizing the endpoint URL, and a private gateway's URL says nothing — a DeepSeek-dialect gateway was spoken to in the OpenAI dialect with no configuration that could correct it. And the only way to touch one catalog model was the `models` list, which *replaces* the served catalog: narrowing `gpt-5`'s levels meant restating all thirty-eight openai models or silently dropping thirty-seven.

Rejected on the bulk case the product's own flow produces: "fetch available models" adopts thirty ids with no modality, and an all-vision gateway would need `input` hand-written on each.

186:| [2026-09-08-bench-e1-sonnet-vs-opus-t5](2026-09-08-bench-e1-sonnet-vs-opus-t5/manifest.json) | `32a2cac6a` | `route`, `sonnet` vs `opus`, sealed | `code:rate-limit-sim` | 2 of 2 vs 2 of 2 | 1 and 2 vs 1 each | 219, 340 s vs 165, 133 s |
288:The thirty-second record is E6, the cascade with a bounded cheap rung, launched at 23:04 UTC on `5ecc68640` and recorded on `9df40295b`, the first experiment run through `pnpm run bench -- experiment` and the first whose arms the service interleaved, so every environment's baseline and candidate cells ran side by side instead of an arm apart: the eight audited tier-5 tasks at two repetitions, seed 2, sealed, 4,307 s of wall time at two cells at a time, the baseline `opus` on three rungs against a candidate whose first rung is `haiku` held to 0.2 of the cell's caps (300,000 billed tokens, 240 s) before `opus`, `opus`, the transcript kept. Both arms certified 16 of 16, so the reading is 0, [0, 0], `inconclusive` by construction. The share did what it was built for: it cut the cheap rung in 14 of 16 cells, 13 at the token share and one at the wall share, as `budget/breach` events scoped to the attempt that blocked no goal, and no cell breached the cell's own caps; the cheap rung certified one cell alone (lex-states, in 129 s), and the strong rung certified the other fifteen, thirteen at the second attempt and two (build-schedule and diff3-merge, one repetition each) at the third. Against the handoff-tax record of 2026-09-08, where the same cascade unbounded certified 14 of 16, the share recovers the two lost certificates; against the strong model alone it recovers none of the cost: 5,618 s of cell time (median 357 s) against 2,802 (median 146 s), 458,300 output tokens against 208,948, 9,231,899 cache-read against 2,542,311, 10,376,073 billed against 2,879,668, because the strong rung's work after the hand-off is a full attempt and the cheap rung's 300,000 tokens buy a certificate in one cell of sixteen. The census finds six cells naming a path outside their workspace in thirteen tool calls, five of them the run directory or a sibling, and no read denied.
292:The thirtieth record is the drop arm run as a fleet under the fixed overlay, launched at 17:43 UTC, eighty minutes after its baseline: the same 16 cells, seed 2, the same ladder, every rung a fresh in-process child of the runner's process on the rung's model with the task restated and the directive carried, the same caps, 5,816 s of wall time at two cells at a time. It certified 14 of 16: 2 at the first rung by the smallest model (ranked-choice, both repetitions), 11 at the second rung by the largest, and 1 at the third (diff3-merge); its two misses (conf-canon and sheet-eval, one repetition each) never reached the strong rung, because the smallest model's single attempt had spent 1,493,040 and 1,472,984 of the cell's 1,500,000 billed tokens rereading its own transcript, and the runner refused the second rung on the breached cap. Folded offline against the twenty-ninth's baseline arm ([folds/2026-09-08-e5-drop-against-kept-transcript-t5.json](folds/2026-09-08-e5-drop-against-kept-transcript-t5.json)), the reading is 0.1875, [0.0625, 0.3125], `promote` by the fold's thresholds: three cells flipped, all toward the fresh child and all on the three tasks the kept transcript failed (build-schedule, conf-canon, sheet-eval), none the other way, with both arms' first rungs at 2 of 16. The fresh child is not cheaper: 575,350 output tokens against 471,583, 16,648,949 billed against 14,911,342, 11,377 s of cell time (median 678 s) against 6,964 (median 441), because every rung reads the task and the workspace from nothing; what it buys is a strong rung that starts from the workspace and the directive instead of from the cheap model's transcript. The fold is offline: its arms ran an hour apart on the shared subscription and were not frozen together, so it is evidence for the slate's prediction that dropping the cheap transcript beats keeping it, not a promotion; the frozen pair on the fixed overlay and a per-rung share of the token cap are queued. The usage of a delegated cell is summed over its `environment/delegation` events, which carry each child's reported model and usage; the census finds no cell leaving its workspace and no read denied.
296:The twenty-eighth record is the held-out reliability estimate the program was to end on: one fleet of the middle model on the harness loop over the eight held-out environments (three at tier 2, three at tier 3, two at tier 5), which no audit, prompt fix, overlay, or fold of this program had touched, seed 3, two repetitions, 16 cells, 2,299 s of wall time at two cells at a time, on the sealed composition ([cordis.yml](../../examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/proving-ground-bench/cordis.yml)) under its three-attempt bound. It certified 15 of 16, every one at the first attempt; the one miss is glob-brace at repetition 0, which ran all three attempts out in 1,270 s while its sibling passed at the first attempt in 473 s, so the four tier-5 cells read 3 of 4 and the twelve cells of tiers 2 and 3 read 12 of 12. The cells took 4,543 s in all (median 210 s), 195 steps, 363,264 output tokens, and 586,558 cache-write tokens. The observatory withholds all eight rows, as it withholds held-out rows from every page ([observatory.json](2026-09-08-bench-held-out-sonnet-all/observatory.json): eight held-out rows over sixteen sessions), so the number is read from the fleet report and the session logs, and it stands as the untuned estimate of the harness loop on this model: 15 of 16 on tasks nothing in the program had seen, beside 13 to 15 of 16 on the audited tier-5 eight; the two sets differ in tier, so only the tier-5 cells' 3 of 4 speaks to the audited difficulty. The census finds one cell leaving its workspace in one tool call, reaching only the parent directory and naming neither the run directory nor a sibling, and no read denied.
306:The twenty-third record is the attempt hypothesis as one frozen paired experiment, which the attempt ladder made possible: the runner takes a ladder's length as a run's attempt bound, so the baseline arm ladders three rungs of the middle model and the candidate one rung of the same model on the same route, and the two arms differ in exactly the cap, with no overlay and no offline fold. Over the eight audited tier-5 environments, seed 2, two repetitions, 32 cells, 5,666 s of wall time at two cells at a time, on the sealed composition with continuity, the three-attempt arm certified 15 of 16 (12 at the first attempt, build-schedule, diff3-merge, and lex-states once each at the second, sheet-eval missed once after three) and the one-attempt arm 9 of 16, delta −0.375, interval [−0.5625, −0.1875], verdict reject for the cap of one: the interval clears the 0.0625 noise floor six times over, and it is the first frozen verdict on record about a mechanism of the harness rather than a model. Read the difference in two parts. Three of the sixteen certificates came at a second attempt after a clustered directive, which is the −0.1875 the counterfactual fold of the eleventh record predicted and exactly what a cap of one forfeits. The other three come from the first attempts themselves: the one-attempt arm's first attempts certified 9 of 16 where the three-attempt arm's certified 12, and the first attempt is the same delivery under either ladder (the task statement alone, nothing about the cap reaches the model), so that part is run-to-run variation of first attempts, not an effect of the cap. Cell by cell the two arms' first attempts disagree on nine of sixteen (three the baseline missed and the candidate made, six the other way), while the final outcomes of two three-attempt runs of this arm disagree on one or two; the loop's value is that it absorbs first-attempt variance the tasks produce whatever the cap, and a single-attempt reading of any model on this bench is a noisier instrument than the three-attempt one by that margin. The cap did not buy speed: 5,689 s of cell time against 5,400 (medians 295 s against 300), 240 model steps against 219, 441,504 output tokens against 402,346, so the two later attempts cost 289 s and 39,158 output tokens over sixteen cells for six more certificates. The census finds eight cells naming their parent or the run directory in twelve tool calls, every one answered by the empty sealed directory, and no read denied.
308:The twenty-second record is the eighteenth rerun as the slate meant it: the harness loop as the baseline arm against the product's own loop as the candidate, the same middle model on both, over the eight audited tier-5 environments, seed 2, two repetitions, 32 cells, 7,235 s of wall time at two cells at a time, on the sealed composition with session continuity on the route and, for the first time, the same caps on both arms: 1,500,000 billed tokens (input plus cache read plus cache write, as the budget policy bills every route) and 1,200,000 ms of wall time per cell, applied to a delegated attempt as to the harness's own. The harness loop certified 15 of 16 (14 at the first attempt, conf-canon once at the third, sheet-eval missed once after three attempts); the product loop 14 of 16, every one at its first attempt, delta −0.0625, interval [−0.125, 0], verdict inconclusive, and the delta is one flip, inside the noise floor the twenty-first record measured. What the parity changed is visible in the two product misses: lex-states breached the token cap after one attempt (1,786,072 billed tokens measured against 1,500,000) and sheet-eval the wall cap (1,202,455 ms against 1,200,000), so neither got the second attempt the eighteenth record's uncapped product arm took, and the cell the product loop had recovered there was not recovered here. Under the same caps the harness loop was the faster arm in 15 of 16 pairs, 5,740 s of cell time against 8,187 (medians 255 s against 422), and the cheaper one: 447,289 output tokens and 7,695,132 billed tokens against 625,239 output and 25,817,220 billed on the product side, where the product reported 14.72 USD for its fifteen attempts that reported usage at all. Three of the harness loop's sealed runs on these cells now stand at 15, 14, and 13 of 16, one or two flips apart; the product loop's two runs at 14 and 11, the second of them uncapped and unsealed. Read with the eighth record and the tier-2 and tier-4 fleets, the harness loop is never worse than the product loop on certificates and is faster at tier 2 and tier 5, slower at tier 4, and the difference it makes is not in certificates but in what surrounds them: the caps hold, the record is complete, and the cell is sealed. The census finds seven harness cells naming their parent or the run directory in eight tool calls, every one answered by the empty sealed directory, and no read denied; the product's child runs outside the harness log, so its own calls are not censused.
314:The nineteenth record is the harness assessing itself through its own program workflow: one department on the route, the largest product model, reading an eleven-file evidence dossier in its worktree (this README, the census, the record index, the last thirty hours of commits, the slate, the roles matrix, the sealed-cell note, the ruflo and baselines comparisons, and the question with the four goals) and writing `assessment.md`, certified by a committed verifier that requires four named sections, two verdict lines, at least eight evidence bullets each citing a dossier file that exists, six distinct files, and 600 to 2,500 words; the integration re-ran the verifier on the merged head. The department certified at its first validation after eleven steps (14 evidence bullets, 9 files cited, 2,258 words) with `Viable: undetermined (medium confidence)` and `State of the art: in part (medium confidence)`, the part being the measurement instrument and its enforcement rather than any measured capability; it also found that this lab's own summary table carries no contamination column and that the tier 2 to 4 comparisons are folds of separate fleets, not frozen experiments. The run exposed three defects in the program workflow, all kept in the artefacts directory beside the record ([2026-09-08-self-assessment-program-artefacts/manifest.json](2026-09-08-self-assessment-program-artefacts/manifest.json)): the department certified with the file written but never committed, so the integration merged an empty branch and failed on `missing assessment.md`; the integration agent, unconfined, then found the department's worktree and rewrote sentences of the certified file with a script before the operator stopped it after 22 steps; and the resume refused to republish the integration session's identity, so the operator committed the department tree as it then stood, set the first integration session aside, and resumed, after which the integration certified the merged head and the program released. The text the department certified is reconstructed byte for byte from its own session's write (`assessment.certified.md`, 2,258 words) and differs from the merged text in five lines, none of them a verdict.
344:The fourth record is the Proving Ground bench's first fleet (`examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/proving-ground-bench/`, thirty admitted program tasks): the product's own loop as the implementer of every cell, over the six tier-2 environments that are not held out, two repetitions each, seed 1, policy `bench-2026-09-07`, district `bench-h1`, two cells at a time, 984 s of wall time for the twelve cells. Every cell was certified in one attempt, so tier 2 is a ceiling for this implementer and the paired comparisons between the harness loop and the product loop run on tiers 3 and 4. The cells name the model `sonnet`; the product ran the installation's default model, which was measured as sonnet immediately before the run, because the delegation did not yet forward the cell's model to the child (the slice that forwards it and records the child's reported model is queued). The bench composition and tasks are those of commit `128e037bb`; the manifest records the head of the working tree at recording time.

# Proving Ground runs

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Records of real Proving Ground runs: the district's certified measurements of one implementer on registered environments, kept exactly as the harness folded and exported them. A run directory is the output of one fleet plan: the cell session logs, the exported session facts, the curator-gated trajectory export, the observatory snapshot and page, the driver's report, and a manifest with every file's digest. Nothing in a run directory is edited after the run; the table below is read from those files.

## Layout

```
data/proving-ground/
  <date>-<implementer>-run-<n>/
    manifest.json        repository head, composition, implementer, session ids, per-file bytes and SHA-256
    result.json          the driver's report: fleet report, delegation records, export reports, observatory document
    facts.jsonl          scorekeeper facts, one per cell session
    trajectories.jsonl   curator-gated trajectory export, one per exported session
    observatory.json     the observatory snapshot the page was rendered from
    observatory.html     the rendered observatory page
    sessions/            the cell session logs, one JSONL file per cell, named by session id
  folds/<date>-<candidate>-against-<baseline>-<tier>.json   an offline paired fold of two recorded fleets that differ by a composition overlay, or a counterfactual of one recorded fleet re-read under a cap
  folds/<date>-<reading>-<tier>-seed<seed>.json             an offline reading over recorded arms that share a tier and seed: the routing reading (oracle and cascades over single-model arms) or the repeatability of one arm across its runs
  datasets/<name>/                                          one fold of every record's trajectories into train.jsonl, heldout.jsonl, and a manifest of the counts, distributions, and digests (see its own README)
  dashboard.html                                            the Proving Ground dashboard, one self-contained page folded from every record and fold above by tools/build-dashboard.mjs
  dashboard.png                                             that page at desktop width as it stood when it was last rebuilt, the image the repository's front page shows
```

## Running one

A run is a Loader-booted composition under `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/` driven from an empty directory outside the repository; the driver creates the session store there and writes the exports next to it. The first run used the composition below, with the host's own Claude Code installation and account as the implementer of every cell:

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/proving-ground-run && cd /tmp/proving-ground-run
REPO=/path/to/deepseek-harness
TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH=$REPO/tsconfig.json node --import $REPO/node_modules/tsx/dist/esm/index.mjs $REPO/examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-claude-implementer/driver.ts $REPO/examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-claude-implementer/cordis.yml > stdout.jsonl
```

Then record it, which copies the exports, every session log, and the driver's result into a new run directory, writes its `manifest.json` with the repository head, the composition, the implementers read from the run stamps, and every file's digest, and refuses to overwrite a recorded run; add a row below afterwards:

```sh
node data/proving-ground/tools/record-run.mjs /tmp/proving-ground-run 2026-09-06-claude-code-run-2 --composition examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-live/cordis.yml
```

A live district (`examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-live/`) is recorded the same way from the directory its driver runs in, one slot per run directory: the shift ledger session lands beside the cell sessions and `result.json` holds the driver's status.

## What a row proves

A delegated cell's certificate proves that the runner authored the standard before any work started, restored the immutable paths from the fixture over the tree the external agent left, found the check-owned set unchanged, and ran the checks itself. It proves nothing about how the work was done: the external agent's prompts, tool calls, and reasoning stay in its own product, so the cell session holds the stamp, the standard, the delegation records, the runs, and the certificate, and no assistant turn. The exported trajectory therefore carries no step. It is a measurement, not training data, and the `implementer` field on the stamp is what a curated export filters on. The [external implementer note](../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-06-external-implementer.md) owns these rules.

## What a cell reached outside its workspace

Every record here ran its cells in a sibling layout — each cell workspace directly under the run directory, beside `plan.json`, the run log, and every other cell of the same fleet — and the records dated 2026-09-08 and earlier ran them unconfined, so nothing stopped a cell from reading any of it. [`tools/census-escapes.mjs`](tools/census-escapes.mjs) reads one record and reports, per cell, the tool calls whose path arguments name the run directory or another cell and the reads the barrier refused; [`tools/record-run.mjs`](tools/record-run.mjs) prints that census, and the per-arm totals below, with every record it writes; a run whose driver died before writing its result is recorded with `--partial <reason>`, which keeps its session logs, states only the reason in its `result.json`, and leaves any verdict to an offline fold under `folds/`. [`tools/summarize-run.mjs`](tools/summarize-run.mjs) reads one record the same way, or a run directory a driver is still writing, and prints, per cell, the arm, the implementer and route, the certificate, the attempts, the wall seconds, the steps, and the usage (a delegated cell's from its delegation records, as the runner reports it), then one line of totals per arm; the certificate counts, attempts, and usage the paragraphs below state are read from it. [`tools/build-dashboard.mjs`](tools/build-dashboard.mjs) folds every record and fold into [`dashboard.html`](dashboard.html), one self-contained page: the verdict of every paired comparison with its interval, the product models on sealed tier 5, the certification rate of every environment under every route, when each record ran, one row per record opening onto its cells and its paragraph here, and the routing and repeatability readings; `--live <run dir>` adds a run a driver is still writing. [`tools/build-dataset.mjs`](tools/build-dataset.mjs) reads every record at once rather than one, folding their trajectories into a dataset under `datasets/<name>/` and refusing to write anything while any trajectory carries a credential- or mailbox-shaped string. Over this corpus the census finds cells that left their own workspace in ten records: 4 of 12 in `2026-09-07-bench-h1-harness-loop-t2`, 11 of 18 in `2026-09-07-bench-h1-harness-loop-t4`, 3 of 36 in `2026-09-07-bench-e2-harness-vs-product-t3`, 8 of 36 in `2026-09-08-bench-e1-haiku-vs-sonnet-t3`, 7 of 36 in `2026-09-08-bench-e1-sonnet-vs-opus-t3`, 6 of 32 in `2026-09-08-bench-e2-harness-vs-product-t5`, 7 of 18 in `2026-09-08-bench-e3-attempts1-t3`, 3 of 18 in `2026-09-08-bench-e3-baseline-t3`, 15 of 18 in `2026-09-08-bench-e4-knowledge-pack-t3`, and 9 of 16 in `2026-09-08-bench-h1-harness-loop-t5`; the other eight records count none, seven of them because every cell was delegated to the product, where the harness session holds no tool call of its own and the census can see nothing the delegate did, and the eighth because it is a one-cell smoke. Two escapes changed what a row measures: in `2026-09-07-bench-h1-harness-loop-t2` the `code:csv-codec` cell `cell-cUuWY2` ran `cp cell-cUuWY2/src/csv.js cell-R8QtdK/src/csv.js`, putting its own solution into the other repetition of its task, and in `2026-09-08-bench-e2-harness-vs-product-t5` the first `code:sheet-eval` cell `cell-Cr3CtN` wrote its whole solution into the second cell's workspace, `cell-XNKQXT`. A record made under a composition that confines its cells — where the runner denies each cell everything above its own workspace for the length of its run — carries the refusals as `escapesDenied` on every scoreboard and observatory row, so the count is read from the row rather than reconstructed from the log.

1	# Agent Note: A bench tier whose verdict comes from cases the implementer never sees
2	
3	Status: proposed
4	
5	English | [中文](2026-09-07-bench-tier-5-hidden-cases.zh.md)
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	The Proving Ground bench held thirty zero-dependency JavaScript program tasks across tiers 2 to 4, each verified by a test suite that ships inside the task directory. The Claude Code product loop certified 48 of 48 non-held-out cells across all three tiers in one attempt each, between 58 and 406 seconds per cell. A bench that every cell of one implementer passes on the first attempt orders nothing: it cannot separate two implementers, cannot show that a change helped, and cannot price a cell's difficulty.
10	
11	The reason is structural, not a matter of writing harder tasks in the same form. The implementer can read `test/*.test.js` before writing a line, so the task it actually faces is "make these assertions pass", not "implement this specification". Every assertion the suite does not make is behaviour the implementer is free to get wrong, and a suite large enough to close that gap is a suite that hands over the answer. Enlarging the visible suite trades one failure for the other.
12	
13	## Proposal
14	
15	Add tier 5, whose main check is differential against a hidden reference on cases the implementer never sees, and populate it with ten tasks. The verification seam already carries what this needs — `AuthoredCheck` may name `cases: CheckCasesRef` with `caseBodies: CheckCase[]`, the runner appends each case's `argv` to the check's `run` and feeds its `stdin`, digests the compared channels, and the failed-validation directive tells the implementer only how many cases failed and which channels mismatched. Tier 5 uses that seam rather than adding a second one.
16	
17	### Where the cases live
18	
19	A tier-5 `task.json` check gains an optional `"cases": "reference/cases.json"` field. The path must sit under `reference/`, which the runner strips from every workspace overlay and copies under the validator's barrier, so a file named there is unreachable from the implementer's workspace by construction rather than by convention. `register-environments.ts` reads that file at registration, digests each case's `stdout` and `stderr` with `caseChannelDigest(…, ['crlf'])`, and hands the check `cases: checkCasesRef(bodies)` alongside `caseBodies: bodies`. Only the reference reaches the session log; the bodies stay in the validator's reservation.
20	
21	The file is a plain array so it stays readable and regenerable:
22	
23	```json
24	[{ "id": "corner-001", "weight": 3, "argv": ["normalize"], "stdin": "…\n",
25	   "exitCode": 0, "stdout": "…\n", "stderr": "", "channels": ["exit", "stdout", "stderr"] }]
26	```
27	
28	The registrar fails the boot on a malformed file, a duplicate case id, a non-positive weight, an `argv` word that would need shell quoting, a channel outside `exit`, `stdout` and `stderr`, a `stderr` channel with no expected text, and a `cases` path that leaves `reference/`. Every one of those is self-contained in the file, so it fails at load.
29	
30	### What a tier-5 task is
31	
32	Each task is a command, `src/cli.js`, driven by arguments and standard input and judged on its exit code and its two streams. The argument words carry only modes and small integers because the runner appends them to the check's `run` verbatim; everything with structure travels on standard input, which has no quoting rules. Beside the command sits a visible suite of twelve to twenty assertions covering the main paths only, a hidden `reference/src/` solution, a `reference/generate-cases.mjs` that runs that solution over a fixed corpus to produce `reference/cases.json`, and a `src/` stub that fails the visible suite.
33	
34	The corpus is deterministic in both halves: hand-written corner cases at weight 3, and combinations drawn from a seeded linear congruential stream at weight 1. Rerunning a generator rewrites the same bytes, so a case file is a build product of its reference and can be regenerated after a specification change rather than hand-maintained.
35	
36	The rule that keeps this fair is that every hidden case must be arguable from the prompt. A case the prompt does not predict is a trap, not a measurement, and the fix is to state the corner or drop the case. The prompt suffix says so from the other side: a task carrying hidden cases tells the implementer that a validator runs held-back inputs and compares byte for byte, and that the written specification, not the visible suite, is what to implement. Tasks without hidden cases do not carry that sentence, because for them it would be false.
37	
38	### Admission
39	
40	`admit.mjs` gains the two conditions a case file must meet. Every case must reproduce against `reference/src/`, which proves the file describes the reference it claims to describe. At least one case must mismatch against the pre-state, which proves the file measures something the visible suite does not already reach: a case set the stub satisfies in full is a case set that certifies a program nobody wrote. Admission prints the case count per admitted task.
41	
42	### The ten tasks
43	
44	| Task | Domain | Held out | Hidden cases |
45	|---|---|---|---|
46	| `uri-resolve` | parsing | no | 150 |
47	| `glob-brace` | parsing | yes | 170 |
48	| `conf-canon` | parsing | no | 150 |
49	| `build-schedule` | data-structures-algorithms | no | 140 |
50	| `ranked-choice` | data-structures-algorithms | no | 170 |
51	| `sheet-eval` | data-structures-algorithms | no | 150 |
52	| `lex-states` | state-machines | no | 160 |
53	| `rate-limit-sim` | systems | no | 150 |
54	| `diff3-merge` | text | no | 160 |
55	| `wrap-justify` | text | yes | 160 |
56	
57	### The difficulty gate
58	
59	Each task was run once against the product loop in a copy of its directory with `reference/` removed, non-interactively with edits accepted and `node` allowed, under an eight-minute limit, and what the loop left behind was then scored against the visible suite and the hidden cases. The gate is not a certificate: it is the evidence that the tier separates anything at all. Two rounds ran: the first over all ten, the second over the six that had passed every hidden case, after their corpora gained corner cases for the specification points those tasks turn on. Every task's row below reports its shipped corpus, and [SUMMARY.md](../../../../examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/proving-ground-bench/SUMMARY.md) carries the per-task detail.
60	
61	Four of the ten failed at least one hidden case and seven passed their visible suite. Only `lex-states` failed while its visible suite passed, at 158 of 160 cases, which is the shape the tier exists to produce; `glob-brace`, `conf-canon` and `sheet-eval` each ran out of the eight-minute budget with nothing runnable in place, which is a difficulty signal of a blunter kind. The six re-run tasks — `uri-resolve`, `build-schedule`, `ranked-choice`, `rate-limit-sim`, `diff3-merge` and `wrap-justify` — scored every hidden case in both rounds, in 201 to 417 seconds, so the added corners moved nothing for this implementer. Against this loop the tier separates on how much specification a task carries, not yet on how sharp its corners are.
62	
63	### The fairness audit of 2026-09-08
64	
65	Two loops then ran the eight non-held-out tier-5 environments — the harness's own loop and the product's, on the same model — and each certified 11 of 16 cells. Where two independent implementers miss the same case at the same point, the case or the prompt is the suspect, not the implementer, so every failed case was read against its prompt. The rule the tier is built on decides each one: (a) the prompt already fixes the expected output, so the miss is the implementer's; (b) the prompt is silent or admits two readings, so the prompt gains the missing sentence; (c) the reference contradicts the prompt, so the reference changes and `generate-cases.mjs` rewrites the corpus.
66	
67	| Task | Cases | What the case turned on | Decision |
68	|---|---|---|---|
69	| `conf-canon` | corner-009, corner-010 | `e = [,]` expected `invalid value ` with an empty offending word, a trailing space no prompt can state | c |
70	| `conf-canon` | corner-011, corner-012 | a duplicate key inside an inline table expected the bare `x` against a prompt that counts the path from the root | c |
71	| `conf-canon` | corner-021, corner-022 | `a = 1` then `[a]` expected `table a is defined twice` where no header had ever made `a` current | c |
72	| `lex-states` | corner-017, corner-018 | `r"unterminated` is reported at its opening quote by one prompt sentence and at the `r` by the next | b |
73	| `lex-states` | corner-073 | `tokens stats` passes two argument words where the prompt takes exactly one | a |
74	| `sheet-eval` | corner-013 | `MIN` over a range holding text: coerce to numbers, or pick by the stated cross-kind order | b |
75	| `sheet-eval` | corner-023, corner-024 | `=AAA1` and `=A1000`: an address outside the addressable range, or a word the grammar rejects | b |
76	| `sheet-eval` | corner-028 | whether `deps` names the cells of a range the evaluator rejects for its position | b |
77	| `sheet-eval` | corner-063 | `values deps` passes two argument words where the prompt takes exactly one | a |
78	| `diff3-merge` | corner-141 | `merge extra` passes two argument words where the prompt takes exactly one | a |
79	
80	The three `conf-canon` reference changes make its error paths uniform. A value reader that consumed nothing now raises `expected a value` instead of naming an empty word, so no message can end in a space; an inline table now carries its path down from the root, matching what `document.js` already did for a key and for a dot walking through a value; and a `[name]` header over a name holding a non-table now reports `<path> is not a table`, which is what `descend` reports one level deeper and the mirror of `[[name]]`'s `<path> is not an array of tables`, leaving `table <path> is defined twice` for the redeclaration the prompt describes. Six of the 150 cases changed and the generator reproduced the file byte for byte on a rerun. The prompts of `conf-canon`, `lex-states` and `sheet-eval` gained the sentences that make each expected output the only reading; `lex-states`, `sheet-eval` and `diff3-merge` needed no reference or corpus change.
81	
82	The remaining corners of all ten tasks were read for the same four failure classes — an exact message with an empty argument, the column of a token behind a prefix, two applicable diagnoses with no stated precedence, and a bare key where a path was promised. No other message in any corpus carries an empty argument, and `glob-brace`'s `a[b\`, `uri-resolve`'s five components checked in a written order, and `build-schedule`'s line-less `unknown task` each state their own precedence. The recorded fleets ran against the pre-audit cases, so their per-case results predate every change above and re-running them is what will show the audit landed.
83	
84	## Alternatives considered
85	
86	**Enlarge the visible suites.** The straightforward reading of "48 of 48" is that the tasks are too easy, and the cheap answer is more assertions. It fails on its own terms: a suite complete enough to pin the behaviour is a suite that states the behaviour, and the implementer reads it before writing anything. The measurement stays "can you satisfy what you were shown".
87	
88	**Hold back a second visible suite and run it after.** A withheld `test/hidden/*.test.js` copied in by the validator needs no new mechanism. It leaks more than it measures: the failure report would carry assertion text, so a retry hands the implementer the withheld specification one message at a time, and the tier degrades to the visible-suite tier after one attempt. The cased-check directive reports counts and channel names only, which is what makes retries survivable.
89	
90	**Compare against the reference at run time instead of shipping digests.** Running `reference/src/` beside the candidate on freshly drawn inputs would need no case file. It puts the reference in the runner's process during a scored run, gives up the digest binding that makes a case file auditable, and makes a cell's verdict depend on what was drawn that day, so two runs of the same plan are no longer comparable. Frozen cases keep a plan reproducible.
91	
92	**A property-based checker instead of cases.** Invariants over generated inputs catch classes of error a fixed corpus misses. They also require an oracle for every property, which for these tasks is the reference again, and they report a counterexample, which is the leak the withheld-suite alternative already fails on.
93	
94	**Put the case bodies in `task.json`.** One file per task is simpler to read. It would sit in the implementer's workspace, so the whole tier would be visible; `reference/` is the only directory the runner already removes.
95	
96	## Acceptance criteria
97	
98	- The registry equals the task files at forty tasks, and every tier-5 registration carries exactly one cased check whose `cases.count` is at least 80, asserted through `registry-driver.ts` in `proving-ground-bench.e2e.ts`.
99	- `admit.mjs` exits 0 over all forty tasks: every pre-state fails its own suite, every reference passes it, every hidden case reproduces against the reference, and at least one mismatches against the pre-state.
100	- Every generator rewrites its case file byte for byte on a rerun, so a case file is reproducible from its reference.
101	- At least four of the ten tasks fail at least one hidden case on a single product-loop attempt, while the visible suite passes on at least six.
102	
103	## Risks
104	
105	**The gate measures one implementer on one day.** The tier separates the product loop as it stands; a stronger loop, or a longer budget, may certify every cell again and put the bench back where it started. The answer then is more corners in the specifications, not a longer suite, and the case files are regenerable for exactly that.
106	
107	**A case that the prompt does not predict is a trap.** The corpus is large enough that an unstated corner can hide in it, and the implementer sees only a count, so a trap is expensive to diagnose. Admission cannot catch this: it proves the reference agrees with the cases, not that the prompt does. Only reading the prompt against the case list catches it, and that reading has to be redone whenever either changes.
108	
109	**The reference is the specification's only executable copy.** A hidden case is right because the reference is right. A defect in a reference becomes a hidden requirement that no visible test contradicts, and the implementer has no way to argue with it.
110	
111	**An eight-minute limit conflates two failures.** A cell that ran out of budget and a cell that finished something wrong both score as a hidden-case failure, and the two mean different things about the task. The recorded results keep the exit status so the two can be told apart, but the acceptance rule does not distinguish them.
112	
113	**Four references fall short of the 250-line floor** the authoring specification sets for a tier-5 solution: `ranked-choice` at 170, `diff3-merge` at 187, `wrap-justify` at 191, and `rate-limit-sim` at 230. Their specification surface is what the tier trades on, and padding the code would not add any, but the shortfall is a signal that those four have less depth than the other six.
114

environments/order-lifecycle/task.json:5:  "title": "Order state machine with an audit trail and idempotent commands",
environments/order-lifecycle/task.json:6:  "prompt": "Finish the order aggregate in `src/`. `src/index.js` re-exports `STATES`, `COMMAND_TYPES`, `TERMINAL_STATES`, `allowedTypes` and `isTerminal` from `src/machine.js` and `Order` from `src/order.js`; keep that surface. The states are `created`, `paid`, `packed`, `shipped`, `delivered`, `cancelled` and `refunded`; the commands are `addItem`, `removeItem`, `pay`, `pack`, `ship`, `deliver`, `cancel` and `refund`. `created` accepts `addItem`, `removeItem`, `pay` and `cancel`; `paid` accepts `pack` and `cancel`; `packed` accepts `ship` and `cancel`; `shipped` accepts `deliver`; `delivered` accepts `refund`; `cancelled` and `refunded` accept nothing and are the terminal states. `allowedTypes(state)` returns that state's commands in ascending order as a fresh array a caller may mutate, and `isTerminal(state)` reports whether the list is empty; both throw `TypeError` with message `unknown state: <state>` for anything else. The exported lists are frozen.

`new Order({ id, createdAt })` starts an order in `created` with no items, nothing paid and nothing refunded. `id` must be a non-empty string and `createdAt`, which defaults to 0, a non-negative integer; violations throw `TypeError` with messages `init must be an object`, `init.id must be a non-empty string` and `init.createdAt must be a non-negative integer`. The read side exposes `id`, `state`, `items` (ascending by sku), `totalCents` (the sum of quantity times unit price), `paidCents`, `refundedCents`, `clockMs`, `shipment`, `deliveredAt`, the `audit` trail and `snapshot()`, which returns `{ id, state, items, totalCents, paidCents, refundedCents, clockMs, seq }` with `seq` the number of audit entries. Every one of these hands back copies: mutating what a getter returned must not change the order.

`apply(command)` runs one command and returns a plain result instead of throwing for business failures. A command carries a `type`, a non-empty `commandId`, a non-negative integer `at`, and the fields its type needs. A structurally malformed command throws `TypeError` and is not recorded: `command must be an object`, `unknown command type: <type>`, `command must carry a non-empty commandId`, `command must carry a non-negative integer at`. Otherwise the checks run in this order, and the first failure decides the outcome. A `commandId` that has been applied before returns exactly the result recorded for it, with `replayed` set to true, and changes nothing at all. An `at` earlier than `clockMs` is rejected with code `'CLOCK_REGRESSION'`, and its audit entry is stamped with the order's current clock so recorded times never decrease; every other command sets `clockMs` to its `at`. A command the current state does not allow is rejected with `'BAD_STATE'`. Then the command's own fields are checked: a missing or empty `sku`, `carrier`, `tracking` or `reason` gives `'MISSING_FIELD'`, and a `qty`, `unitPriceCents` or `amountCents` that is not an integer in range gives `'BAD_AMOUNT'` (`qty` and a refund `amountCents` must be at least 1; `unitPriceCents` and a payment `amountCents` must be at least 0). Then the business guards: adding a sku that is already present gives `'DUPLICATE_SKU'`, removing one that is not gives `'NO_SUCH_ITEM'`, paying an order with no items gives `'EMPTY_ORDER'`, paying anything other than `totalCents` gives `'AMOUNT_MISMATCH'`, and refunding more than `paidCents - refundedCents` gives `'REFUND_TOO_LARGE'`. A successful result is `{ ok: true, state, seq, replayed }` and a rejection is `{ ok: false, code, message, state, seq, replayed }`, where `message` is a non-empty explanation and `seq` is the audit entry number.

Every command that gets as far as the clock check appends exactly one audit entry, whether it succeeded or not: `{ seq, commandId, type, at, from, to, ok }` plus `code` on a rejection, with `seq` counting from 1, `from` the state before and `to` the state after, so a rejection has `from` equal to `to`. Effects: `addItem` and `removeItem` edit the item list and leave the state at `created`; `pay` records `amountCents` as `paidCents` and moves to `paid`; `pack` moves to `packed`; `ship` records the carrier and tracking and moves to `shipped`; `deliver` records `at` as `deliveredAt` and moves to `delivered`; `cancel` refunds everything captured so far and moves to `cancelled`; `refund` adds to `refundedCents` and moves to `refunded` only once the whole payment has been returned. `refundedCents` never exceeds `paidCents`. The static `Order.replay(init, commands)` builds a fresh order and applies each command in turn, giving the same snapshot and audit trail as applying them one at a time; a non-array argument throws `TypeError`.",

1	# Agent Note: Where the four objectives stand, what blocks each, and the order of work
2	
3	Status: proposed
4	
5	English | [中文](2026-09-19-objectives-step-back.zh.md)
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	The project has four objectives: a harness that makes any model the best agentic coder it can be, agentic software creation through that harness, a roughly 120B open-weight model trained by RLVR on the harness's certified runs, and a loop in which the harness improves itself by evidence. Two weeks of building produced the instrument (a 40-environment bench with validator-held cases, sealed cells, frozen paired experiments with bootstrap verdicts, a runner with attempt ladders and budget shares, a program workflow, a trajectory exporter and dataset builder, terms gating, a dashboard) and 32 recorded runs, 920 cells, and 844 certificates ([data/proving-ground](../../../../data/proving-ground/README.md)). What nobody has written down is how far each objective actually is from "partly done", which facts block it, and what order the remaining work should take. Without that, effort keeps flowing to whatever is nearest.
10	
11	## Proposal
12	
13	State the standing of each objective from the records, name the blocker, and take the work in the order below.
14	
15	### Objective 1: the best harness for any model
16	
17	Standing: the instrument exists and discriminates at tier 5 only; the harness has not yet shown a certificate win over the product's own loop, and every one of the 32 records ran one provider's models through the operator's Claude Code login. The paired readings in [the results note](../architecture/2026-09-08-hypothesis-program-results.md) are: the harness loop equals the product loop on certificates at tiers 3 and 5 (0 and −0.0625, both inside the one-flip noise floor) while being faster in 15 of 16 sealed pairs and 3.4 times cheaper in billed tokens; the largest model certifies every sealed tier-5 cell; attempts matter (three against one, +0.375); knowledge packs, craft skills, model cascades, and a dropped transcript add no certificates, and the cascade with a bounded cheap rung (E6) recovers the certificates the unbounded one lost at twice the cost. The bench below tier 5 is saturated by every model, and tier 5 is saturated by the largest one.
18	
19	Blockers: one provider; a top tier the largest model saturates; a noise floor of one to two flips at sixteen pairs.
20	
21	Next: run the bench on a second model family the moment a key exists (the open-weight overlay below); add a tier the largest model does not saturate (multi-file tasks with a repository and a spec, hidden cases held by the validator, the same admission and fairness audit as tier 5); test mechanisms with a stated hypothesis of effect on the middle model at tier 5, one per frozen pair (E7, five attempts against three, is running; then a self-review rung before validation and a directive that carries the validator's channel diff); run two seeds per experiment so a reading has thirty-two pairs.
22	
23	### Objective 2: agentic software creation through the harness
24	
25	Standing: the program workflow (departments in worktrees, integration, committed verifier, commit-or-refuse) has run once for real, producing an assessment document, never a piece of software.
26	
27	Next: the `csv-tools` program (three departments, a spec, a `node:test` verifier) prepared today and run on the route after E7; then a program that builds a plugin for this repository under its own gates, which is the dogfooding case the objective actually means.
28	
29	### Objective 3: the open-weight model trained by RLVR
30	
31	Standing: the pipeline exists and was exercised as a dry run: 750 trajectories in the `dsh-trajectory/1` format, 521 on the harness route, in [the v1 dataset fold](../../../../data/proving-ground/datasets/2026-09-18-proving-ground-v1/README.md), with rewards from certificates and parity. Not one of them may train the Daliesk model: all ran on the operator's Claude Code login, and the [data-use terms](../../../../packages/governance/data-use/README.md) admit into the training corpus only sessions pinned with terms that allow it, which only a route on an open-weight model can carry. The corpus that matters is therefore empty, and no training compute is attached to this repository.
32	
33	Blockers, in order: a key for an open-weight route (`DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` for [`dsh-llm-deepseek`](../../../../packages/llm/llm-deepseek/README.md), or a gateway key through [`dsh-llm-pi-ai`](../../../../packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/README.md)); the base-model decision, still open; compute for the RLVR run itself.
34	
35	Next, without a key: the `with-deepseek` and gateway overlays with their plans, so the bench runs on an open model one environment variable after the key arrives, and the corpus fills from those runs alone; the training recipe as a proposed note (certified trajectories as the SFT warm-up, the validator as the RLVR reward over the same environments, held-out environments as the only reported number). With a key: the tier-2 fleet first, then the tier-3 frozen pair against the middle product model, recorded like every other run.
36	
37	### Objective 4: the self-improvement loop
38	
39	Standing: every piece exists and has run (frozen pairs, the verdict rule, composition manifests, the program workflow), but each iteration was proposed by a person, launched by hand through `pnpm run bench`, and applied by editing a composition. The iterations are legible only across a note, thirty-two records, and ten folds.
40	
41	Next: the improvement log under `data/proving-ground/` as the ledger of every iteration with its verdict and decision (today), then the propose step inside the harness (a department reads the ledger and the bench's misses and writes a candidate overlay and plan), scheduled launches through the shift driver, and promotion through the composition manifest rather than a hand edit.
42	
43	### Order of work
44	
45	Today: E7 recorded; the open-weight overlays, plans, and keyless refusal; the improvement log; the `csv-tools` program run and recorded; the dashboard and this note updated. Next: the tier above tier 5; the self-review rung as a frozen pair; the propose step. Needed from the operator: a key for an open-weight route in the environment, a decision on training compute, and the base model.
46	
47	## Alternatives considered
48	
49	- Keep running experiments on the one provider until an effect appears. Rejected: the top tier is saturated by the largest model, and no trajectory from that provider can train the model, so the runs would answer neither objective 1 nor 3.
50	- Build the next bench tier before the open-weight route. Deferred: the tier matters most once a second model family runs, and the route is one variable away while the tier is days of authoring and audit.
51	- Call the harness state of the art now. Rejected: on the recorded evidence it equals the product loop on certificates, on one provider, and is cheaper; that is a cost result, not a capability result.
52	
53	## Acceptance criteria
54	
55	- One run on an open-weight route recorded under `data/proving-ground/` with terms that admit training, and the corpus fold counting at least one admitted trajectory.
56	- The `csv-tools` program certified by its verifier and recorded as a program record.
57	- The improvement log carrying E7's verdict and decision.
58	- The next bench tier admitted with the fairness audit, and one frozen pair on it.
59	
60	## Risks
61	
62	- The shared subscription's rate limits and the container's restarts (two on 2026-09-18) can cut a run; the partial-record path keeps what ran.
63	- Sixteen-pair readings invite over-reading; the note's noise-floor rule stands.
64	- A dataset that mixes provider-of-record trajectories into training would breach the terms; the curator withholds them, and the fold's manifest names every source record so a reader can check.

/**
 * Run local and CI quality gates with bounded in-process scheduling.
 *
 * Package scripts own public aggregate names; this runner owns their validated
 * dependency graphs, scheduler environment, and process diagnostics.
 * @see ../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-06-parallel-pre-push-gates.md
 */
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
import { availableParallelism } from 'node:os'
import { resolve } from 'node:path'
import { performance } from 'node:perf_hooks'
import { COVERAGE_EXEMPT_ENV, coverageExemptHeavySuites } from './coverage-exempt.ts'

/** A named aggregate exposed by the gate runner. */
export type Mode =
  | 'ci-primary'
  | 'ci-linux-primary'
  | 'ci-static'
  | 'ci-lint-contracts-ready'
  | 'ci-coverage'
  | 'ci-snapshot'
  | 'ci-artifacts'
  | 'ci-consumers'
  | 'ci-windows-blocking'
  | 'ci-windows-complete'
  | 'ci-windows-observational'
  | 'node-compat'
  | 'check-all'
  | 'doc-sync'

type GateResultStatus = 'passed' | 'failed' | 'skipped'
type GateState = 'pending' | 'running' | GateResultStatus

/** A command and its dependency metadata inside one aggregate. */
export interface Gate {
  id: string
  label: string
  displayCommand: string
  command: string
  args: string[]
  needs?: string[]
  env?: Record<string, string | undefined>
  allowFailure?: boolean
}

/** The observed outcome of one gate process. */
export interface GateResult {
  gate: Gate
  status: GateResultStatus
  durationMs: number
  output: GateOutputChunk[]
  exitCode: number | null
  signalCode: NodeJS.Signals | null
  error?: string
}

interface GateOutputChunk {
  stream: 'stdout' | 'stderr'
  text: string
}

interface RunningGate {
  gate: Gate
  promise: Promise<GateResult>
}

interface ConcurrencyDefault {
  workers: number
  source: string
}

type GateExecutor = (gate: Gate) => Promise<GateResult>
type ResultObserver = (result: GateResult) => void

const root = resolve(import.meta.dirname, '..')
if (import.meta.main) {
  process.exitCode = await main(process.argv.slice(2))
}

async function main(args: string[]): Promise<number> {
  const mode = parseMode(args[0])
  const gates = gatesForMode(mode)
  const concurrencyDefault = defaultConcurrency(mode, gates.length)
  const concurrencyOverride = process.env.DSH_GATE_CONCURRENCY
  const maxConcurrency = concurrencyFromEnv('DSH_GATE_CONCURRENCY', concurrencyDefault.workers)
  const concurrencySource = concurrencyOverride === undefined || concurrencyOverride === ''
    ? concurrencyDefault.source
    : '$DSH_GATE_CONCURRENCY'
  const startedAt = performance.now()
  console.log(`run-gates: ${mode} running ${gates.length} gate(s) with ${maxConcurrency} worker(s) from ${concurrencySource}.`)

  const results = await runGates(gates, maxConcurrency, runGate, printResult)
  printSummary(results, performance.now() - startedAt)
  return results.some(result => result.gate.allowFailure !== true && (result.status === 'failed' || result.status === 'skipped'))
    ? 1
    : 0
}

function parseMode(raw: string | undefined): Mode {
  switch (raw) {
    case 'ci-primary':
    case 'ci-linux-primary':
    case 'ci-static':
    case 'ci-lint-contracts-ready':
    case 'ci-coverage':
    case 'ci-snapshot':
    case 'ci-artifacts':
    case 'ci-consumers':
    case 'ci-windows-blocking':
    case 'ci-windows-complete':
    case 'ci-windows-observational':
    case 'node-compat':
    case 'check-all':
    case 'doc-sync':
      return raw
    default:
      throw new Error(
        `run-gates: expected mode ci-primary | ci-linux-primary | ci-static | ci-lint-contracts-ready | ci-coverage | ci-snapshot | ci-artifacts | ci-consumers | ci-windows-blocking | ci-windows-complete | ci-windows-observational | node-compat | check-all | doc-sync, got ${JSON.stringify(raw)}.`,
      )
  }
